newsitem.title: UK: Copper nervy on LME, market drifts towards $2,350.
newsitem.headline: Copper nervy on LME, market drifts towards $2,350.

text.p: Copper trading got off to a nervous start on the LME on Tuesday as the market tried to settle down after Monday's volatile activity, and prices were hovering just above $2,350.
Traders said sentiment was uncertain, following the dramatic collapse in the spread backwardation which took place in the previous session.
Cash/threes was indicated at $80/90 backwardation, having been as high as $210 at one stage on Monday.
But despite the wave of lending, and talk that the major positions have either been rolled forward or switched, copper remains highly susceptible to further tightness flaring up, they said.
"Nothing has changed on the fundamentals...and in any move up you always get a technical re-tracement of say 50 percent," one said.

Escondida miners are still striking in Chile, another Chilean mine at Quebrada Blanca will be striking on Wednesday, the Kennecott smelter is temporarily closed, and a long-running dispute at Phelps Dodge's Chino facilities remains unresolved.
Also, stock levels continue to fall, although Tuesday's decline in inventories was a modest 725 tonnes.
Some initial stop-loss selling unsettled the forward market, which eased to $2,354, down $2. If $2,350 is breached the downside target is $2,320/30.
Other metals traded slowly, keeping a weather-eye on the copper market, although there was an undercurrent of steadiness in aluminium.
Aluminium rose to $1,633, up $4.50 from Monday after a 2,475-tonne stock fall. Early-July tightness, reflecting technical factors, is underscoring the market, they said.
Zinc slipped by $1 to $1,266 amid some caution over inventory movements. Stocks dropped 175 tonnes but there is talk of Chinese metal heading for Singapore.
Nickel dropped $70 to $7,390, while tin shed $$20 to $5,695.
Lead and alloy were quiet and indicated at $628/630 and $1,447/52 per tonne respectively.
